title: Responsive behaviour
learningObjectives: Complete responsive behaviour using the project's existing HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and engineering practices.

understand.concept: Responsive behaviour adapts layout and content to available space using flexible sizing, wrapping, media queries, and component-aware patterns. The design should preserve reading order and functionality across viewports and zoom levels.
understand.whyItMatters: A responsive page must support real content, long labels, and different input contexts, not just match one device screenshot.
understand.analogy: Responsive design is furniture that rearranges to fit the room while keeping every path usable.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; project requirements and release quality must be verified against the actual implementation and user needs.

explain.narrative: The grid fits as many cards as the available width permits without relying on device-specific breakpoints.

examples.explanation: The grid fits as many cards as the available width permits without relying on device-specific breakpoints.
examples.expectedOutput: The example demonstrates a project planning or implementation concept; learners must integrate and test it in their project.

practise.guidedTask: Test the project at narrow, medium, and wide widths and at increased zoom. Fix overflow and preserve logical order.
practise.independentTask: Complete the task in a project repository. Keep the scope explicit, preserve user privacy, test the main workflow, and document evidence and known limitations.
hints: Plan before coding and keep changes focused.
Use semantic HTML and reusable responsive CSS.
Test keyboard access, edge cases, and deployment behaviour.
